newsitem.title: USA: Group advises Cessna owners to check exhausts.
newsitem.headline: Group advises Cessna owners to check exhausts.

text.p: The Cessna Pilots Association has told owners of some twin-engine Cessnas the aircraft have been catching fire at an alarming rate and to correct the problem on their own and not wait for FAA action.

It published on the Internet on Monday a letter sent to owners of turbocharged twin Cessnas earlier this month saying that in the last 29 months at least 29 people have died in a dozen crashes in which exhaust system failure is known or suspected. The CPA advised them to have the exhaust system on the aircraft disassembled and checked, an action it said would affect about 7,000 of the six to 12-seat Cessnas whose uses include corporate travel, light cargo and air tours.
CPA specialist Michael Busch said disassembly had been recommended by the National Transportation Safety Board and such an action was now being considered by the FAA.

Another CPA official said the pilots were not accusing the FAA of foot-dragging, but the letter was only a reflection of the fact that it could put the word out to Cessna owners faster that a U.S. agency with bureaucratic rules to follow.
There was no immediate comment from the FAA or the Cessna Aircraft Co., a unit of Textron Inc.
